decisions.reason: The verb can mean to bear a child or to father one; here the subject is "who", and Zion, who sees herself as abandoned by her husband (54:1, 6), asks where the children came from.

decisions.choice: bereaved and barren, exiled and turned away
decisions.reason: The first pair describes a mother who has lost her children and can have no more; the rare word for barren appears also in Job 3:7. The second pair describes her people carried off and her rejected.

decisions.choice: taken away from my home
decisions.reason: Readable explains "exiled".

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אֶשָּׂ֤א אֶל־גּוֹיִם֙ יָדִ֔י וְאֶל־עַמִּ֖ים אָרִ֣ים נִסִּ֑י וְהֵבִ֤יאוּ בָנַ֨יִךְ֙ בְּחֹ֔צֶן וּבְנֹתַ֖יִךְ עַל־כָּתֵ֥ף תִּנָּשֶֽׂאנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: here! I will lift up to nations my hand, and to peoples I will raise my signal flag; and they will bring your sons in [the] bosom, and your daughters on [the] shoulder will be carried.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: See, I will lift up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to [the] nations, \q and to [the] peoples I will raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} signal flag; \q and they will bring your sons in [their] bosom, \q and your daughters will be carried on [their] shoulder.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: See, I will raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to beckon the nations \q and lift {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} signal flag for the peoples. \q They will carry your sons home in their arms, \q and your daughters will ride on their shoulders.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Look, I will wave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to call the nations. \q I will raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} signal flag so the peoples will see it. \q They will carry your sons back to you in their arms. \q They will carry your daughters on their shoulders.

es.L: Así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Mira, alzaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano hacia las naciones, \q y hacia los pueblos levantaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} bandera; \q y traerán a tus hijos en [su] regazo, \q y tus hijas serán llevadas sobre [sus] hombros.
es.B: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto: Mira, alzaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano para llamar a las naciones \q y levantaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} bandera ante los pueblos. \q Traerán a tus hijos en brazos, \q y tus hijas vendrán sobre sus hombros.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Mira, haré una señal con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano para llamar a las naciones. \q Levantaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} bandera para que los pueblos la vean. \q Te traerán de vuelta a tus hijos en brazos. \q Llevarán a tus hijas sobre los hombros.

fr.L: Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Voici, je lèverai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main vers les nations, \q et vers les peuples je dresserai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} étendard ; \q et ils ramèneront tes fils dans [leurs] bras, \q et tes filles seront portées sur [leurs] épaules.
fr.B: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Voici, je lèverai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main pour faire signe aux nations \q et je dresserai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} étendard pour les peuples. \q Ils ramèneront tes fils dans leurs bras, \q et tes filles seront portées sur leurs épaules.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Regarde, je ferai signe de la main pour appeler les nations. \q Je lèverai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} drapeau pour que les peuples le voient. \q Ils te ramèneront tes fils dans leurs bras. \q Ils porteront tes filles sur leurs épaules.

sw.L: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Tazama, nitainua mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kwa mataifa, \q na kwa watu wa mataifa nitaisimamisha bendera {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q nao watawaleta wana wako vifuani [mwao], \q na binti zako watabebwa mabegani [mwao].
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Tazama, nitainua mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kuyaashiria mataifa \q na kusimamisha bendera {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kwa ajili ya watu wa mataifa. \q Watawabeba wana wako mikononi mwao kuwaleta nyumbani, \q na binti zako watabebwa mabegani mwao.
sw.R: Hili ndilo Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} analosema: Tazama, nitapunga mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kuyaita mataifa. \q Nitaisimamisha bendera {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ili watu wa mataifa waione. \q Watawabeba wana wako mikononi mwao na kuwarudisha kwako. \q Watawabeba binti zako mabegani mwao.

decisions.choice: my signal flag: a banner raised on a pole to call people together
decisions.reason: In 11:12 God raises a signal for the nations to gather Israel's scattered people; here the nations themselves carry the children home (also 62:10).

decisions.choice: in the bosom: held against the chest, as a small child is carried
decisions.reason: The word means the fold of a garment at the chest, where a little child was carried (Numbers 11:12).

decisions.choice: to beckon; to call
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why the hand is raised: as a signal to call the nations.

decisions.choice: bandera
decisions.reason: Book-wide for *nes* in this block: "bandera" at every level, "alzar una bandera", as Psalm 60:6 and the terms note.

decisions.choice: bendera yangu
decisions.reason: The signal flag raised on a pole is "bendera", as Psalm 60:6, at every level.

decisions.choice: "mon étendard" (L, B), "mon drapeau" (R)
decisions.reason: *Nes* is "un étendard" at Literal and Balanced and the everyday "un drapeau" at Readable, as settled for Isaiah.

source.text: וְהָי֨וּ מְלָכִ֜ים אֹֽמְנַ֗יִךְ וְשָׂרֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ מֵינִ֣יקֹתַ֔יִךְ אַפַּ֗יִם אֶ֚רֶץ יִשְׁתַּ֣חֲווּ לָ֔ךְ וַעֲפַ֥ר רַגְלַ֖יִךְ יְלַחֵ֑כוּ וְיָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יֵבֹ֖שׁוּ קוָֹֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And will be kings your foster fathers, and their princesses your nursing women; face [to the] ground they will bow down to you, and [the] dust of your feet they will lick; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh, whom not will be ashamed [those] waiting for me.

en.L: And kings will be your guardians, and their princesses your nursing women; \q with face [to the] ground they will bow down to you, \q and the dust of your feet they will lick; \q and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q [I] whose waiting ones will not be ashamed.
en.B: Kings will look after your children as guardians, and their princesses will nurse them for you. \q They will bow low before you with their faces to the ground \q and lick the dust off your feet. \q Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and that none who wait in hope for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} end up ashamed.
en.R: Kings will take care of your children like fathers. Princesses will feed them like mothers. \q They will bow down to you with their faces to the ground. \q They will lie low in the dust in front of you. \q Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q People who wait for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with hope will never be let down.

es.L: Y reyes serán tus ayos, y sus princesas tus nodrizas; \q con el rostro [en] tierra se postrarán ante ti, \q y el polvo de tus pies lamerán; \q y sabrás que yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q [y que] no serán avergonzados los que me esperan.
es.B: Los reyes cuidarán de tus hijos como tutores, y sus princesas los criarán por ti. \q Se postrarán ante ti con el rostro en tierra \q y lamerán el polvo de tus pies. \q Entonces sabrás que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q y que ninguno de los que esperan en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} acaba avergonzado.
es.R: Los reyes cuidarán de tus hijos como padres. Las princesas los alimentarán como madres. \q Se inclinarán ante ti con el rostro en el suelo. \q Se echarán en el polvo delante de ti. \q Entonces sabrás que yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q Los que esperan en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} con esperanza nunca quedarán defraudados.

fr.L: Et des rois seront tes tuteurs, et leurs princesses tes nourrices ; \q le visage contre terre, ils se prosterneront devant toi, \q et ils lécheront la poussière de tes pieds ; \q et tu sauras que je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q et ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}attendent ne seront pas couverts de honte.
fr.B: Des rois prendront soin de tes enfants comme des tuteurs, et leurs princesses les nourriront pour toi. \q Ils se prosterneront devant toi, le visage contre terre, \q et lécheront la poussière de tes pieds. \q Alors tu sauras que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q et que ceux qui espèrent en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne sont jamais déçus.
fr.R: Des rois s’occuperont de tes enfants comme des pères. Des princesses les nourriront comme des mères. \q Ils se prosterneront devant toi, le visage contre terre. \q Ils se courberont jusque dans la poussière devant toi. \q Alors tu sauras que je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Ceux qui espèrent en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne seront jamais déçus.

sw.L: Na wafalme watakuwa walezi wako, na malkia wao wauguzi wako; \q kwa nyuso [hadi] chini watakusujudia, \q na mavumbi ya miguu yako wataramba; \q nawe utajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q [ambaye] wanaonisubiri hawataaibika.
sw.B: Wafalme watawatunza watoto wako kama walezi, na malkia wao watawanyonyesha kwa ajili yako. \q Watasujudu mbele yako nyuso zao zikiwa chini \q na kuramba mavumbi ya miguu yako. \q Ndipo utajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q na kwamba hakuna anayenisubiri kwa matumaini atakayeaibika.
sw.R: Wafalme watawatunza watoto wako kama baba. Malkia watawalisha kama mama. \q Watakusujudia nyuso zao zikiwa chini. \q Watalala chini mavumbini mbele yako. \q Ndipo utajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Watu wanaonisubiri kwa matumaini hawatavunjika moyo kamwe.

decisions.choice: guardians and nursing women: royal figures caring for Zion's children
decisions.reason: The first word is used of a man who carries and cares for a child (Numbers 11:12) and of the guardians of a king's sons (2 Kings 10:1, 5). The second is a wet nurse, a woman who breastfeeds another's child.

decisions.choice: faces to the ground, licking the dust of your feet: complete submission
decisions.reason: The same picture of conquered rulers is in Psalm 72:9 and Micah 7:17. The kings who once ruled Zion now honor her (compare verse 7).

decisions.choice: those who wait for me will not be ashamed: hope in God is not disappointed
decisions.reason: To wait for God is to hope in him and keep trusting (40:31). Being put to shame means finding one's hope was misplaced (Psalm 25:3).

decisions.choice: lie low in the dust in front of you
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of licking the dust as bowing as low as possible.

source.text: הֲיֻקַּ֥ח מִגִּבּ֖וֹר מַלְק֑וֹחַ וְאִם־שְׁבִ֥י צַדִּ֖יק יִמָּלֵֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: Will be taken from a warrior plunder, or [the] captives of a righteous [one] escape?

en.L: Can plunder be taken from a warrior, \q or can the captives of a righteous [one] escape?
en.B: Can loot be pulled from a warrior's grasp? \q Can captives held by one who is in the right get free?
en.R: Can anyone take back what a strong soldier has captured? \q Can prisoners escape from someone who has the right to hold them?

es.L: ¿Se quitará el botín al valiente, \q o escaparán los cautivos del justo?
es.B: ¿Se le puede arrancar el botín de las manos a un guerrero? \q ¿Pueden librarse los cautivos de quien los tiene con derecho?
es.R: ¿Puede alguien recuperar lo que un soldado fuerte ha capturado? \q ¿Pueden escapar los prisioneros de alguien que tiene derecho a retenerlos?

fr.L: Le butin sera-t-il pris au guerrier, \q ou les captifs d’un juste s’échapperont-ils ?
fr.B: Peut-on arracher le butin des mains d’un guerrier ? \q Les captifs de celui qui est dans son droit peuvent-ils s’enfuir ?
fr.R: Quelqu’un peut-il reprendre ce qu’un soldat puissant a capturé ? \q Des prisonniers peuvent-ils s’échapper des mains de quelqu’un qui a le droit de les garder ?

sw.L: Je, mateka yanaweza kunyang'anywa shujaa, \q au wafungwa wa [mtu] mwenye haki wanaweza kuponyoka?
sw.B: Je, nyara zinaweza kunyakuliwa kutoka mikononi mwa shujaa? \q Je, wafungwa wanaoshikiliwa na mwenye haki wanaweza kuwa huru?
sw.R: Je, kuna mtu anayeweza kurudisha kile ambacho askari hodari ameteka? \q Je, wafungwa wanaweza kutoroka kutoka kwa mtu mwenye haki ya kuwashikilia?

decisions.choice: the captives of a righteous one: captives held by right
decisions.reason: The Masoretic Text has "righteous", which may mean a captor who holds his prisoners lawfully. The Great Isaiah Scroll reads "a ruthless one" (from memory; to be checked), the same word as in verse 25, and the Syriac and Latin translations agree with it (from memory; to be checked). The Masoretic Text is followed here. Either way the question expects the answer no: such captives are not normally set free.

decisions.choice: can plunder be taken ... or can captives escape: questions that expect "no"
decisions.reason: Zion, or a listener, doubts that captives can be freed from such power. Verse 25 answers the doubt.

source.text: כִּי־כֹ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה גַּם־שְׁבִ֤י גִבּוֹר֙ יֻקָּ֔ח וּמַלְק֥וֹחַ עָרִ֖יץ יִמָּלֵ֑ט וְאֶת־יְרִיבֵךְ֙ אָנֹכִ֣י אָרִ֔יב וְאֶת־בָּנַ֖יִךְ אָנֹכִ֥י אוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh: even [the] captives of a warrior will be taken, and [the] plunder of a ruthless [one] will escape; and with your opponent I, I will contend, and your children I, I will save.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Even the captives of a warrior will be taken, \q and the plunder of a ruthless [one] will escape; \q and with your opponent I, I will contend, \q and your children I, I will save.
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Yes, a warrior's captives will be taken from him, \q and a tyrant's loot will slip out of his hands. \q I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will take on the one who fights you, \q and I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will rescue your children.
en.R: But this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Yes, prisoners will be taken back from strong soldiers. \q What cruel people have stolen will be rescued. \q I will fight against anyone who fights against you. \q I will save your children.

es.L: Porque así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Aun los cautivos del valiente serán quitados, \q y el botín del tirano escapará; \q y con el que contiende contigo yo, yo contenderé, \q y a tus hijos yo, yo salvaré.
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Sí, al guerrero le quitarán sus cautivos, \q y el botín se le escapará de las manos al tirano. \q Yo mismo me enfrentaré al que pelea contigo, \q y yo mismo rescataré a tus hijos.
es.R: Pero esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Sí, a los soldados fuertes se les quitarán los prisioneros. \q Lo que la gente cruel ha robado será rescatado. \q Pelearé contra cualquiera que pelee contra ti. \q Salvaré a tus hijos.

fr.L: Car ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Même les captifs du guerrier seront pris, \q et le butin du tyran s’échappera ; \q et avec ton adversaire, moi, je contesterai, \q et tes fils, moi, je les sauverai.
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Oui, les captifs seront arrachés au guerrier, \q et le butin échappera aux mains du tyran. \q C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} qui affronterai celui qui te combat, \q et c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}} qui sauverai tes enfants.
fr.R: Mais voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Oui, des prisonniers seront repris aux soldats puissants. \q Ce que des gens cruels ont volé sera sauvé. \q Je combattrai tous ceux qui te combattent. \q Je sauverai tes enfants.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Hata wafungwa wa shujaa watachukuliwa, \q na mateka ya mkatili yataponyoka; \q na mshindani wako {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitashindana naye, \q na watoto wako {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitawaokoa.
sw.B: Lakini hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Naam, wafungwa wa shujaa watachukuliwa kutoka kwake, \q na nyara za dhalimu zitamponyoka mikononi. \q Mimi {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitapambana na yule anayepigana nawe, \q na {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitawaokoa watoto wako.
sw.R: Lakini hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Naam, wafungwa watachukuliwa tena kutoka kwa askari hodari. \q Kile ambacho watu wakatili wameiba kitaokolewa. \q Nitapigana na yeyote anayepigana nawe. \q Nitawaokoa watoto wako.

decisions.choice: for, but: God answers the doubt of verse 24
decisions.reason: The small word that opens the verse gives the reason the doubt is wrong. What cannot happen by human power will happen because God acts.

decisions.choice: your opponent ... I will contend: God takes up Zion's dispute
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a quarrel or lawsuit and also for open conflict (3:13; 41:11; 50:8). God himself takes on whoever opposes Zion.

decisions.choice: I, I: the pronoun is stressed twice
decisions.reason: God puts himself forward: he himself will fight, and he himself will save.

source.text: וְהַאֲכַלְתִּ֤י אֶת־מוֹנַ֨יִךְ֙ אֶת־בְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְכֶעָסִ֖יס דָּמָ֣ם יִשְׁכָּר֑וּן וְיָדְע֣וּ כָל־בָּשָׂ֗ר כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ אֲבִ֥יר יַעֲקֹֽב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will make eat those oppressing you their own flesh, and like sweet wine their own blood they will be drunk; and will know all flesh that I [am] Yahweh your Savior and your Redeemer, [the] Mighty One of Jacob.

en.L: And I will make those who oppress you eat their own flesh, \q and as with sweet wine they will be drunk with their own blood; \q and all flesh will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, your Savior, \q and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
en.B: Those who oppress you I will feed with their own flesh, \q and they will get drunk on their own blood as if it were new wine. \q Then all humankind will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am the one who saves you, \q your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
en.R: I will make the people who hurt you destroy themselves, as if they were eating their own flesh \q and getting drunk on their own blood like wine. \q Then everyone on earth will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am the one who saves you. \q I am your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

es.L: Y haré que los que te oprimen coman su propia carne, \q y como con mosto se embriagarán con su propia sangre; \q y sabrá toda carne que yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, tu Salvador, \q y tu Redentor, el Poderoso de Jacob.
es.B: A los que te oprimen les daré a comer su propia carne, \q y se emborracharán con su propia sangre como si fuera vino nuevo. \q Entonces toda la humanidad sabrá que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, soy el que te salva, \q tu Redentor, el Poderoso de Jacob.
es.R: Haré que los que te hacen daño se destruyan a sí mismos, como si se comieran su propia carne \q y se emborracharan con su propia sangre como con vino. \q Entonces todos en la tierra sabrán que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, soy el que te salva. \q Soy tu Redentor, el Poderoso de Jacob.

fr.L: Et je ferai manger à tes oppresseurs leur propre chair, \q et comme du vin doux ils s’enivreront de leur propre sang ; \q et toute chair saura que je [suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ton Sauveur, \q et ton Rédempteur, le Puissant de Jacob.
fr.B: Tes oppresseurs, je les nourrirai de leur propre chair, \q et ils s’enivreront de leur propre sang comme de vin nouveau. \q Alors tous les humains sauront que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je suis celui qui te sauve, \q ton Libérateur, le Puissant de Jacob.
fr.R: Je ferai que les gens qui te font du mal se détruisent eux-mêmes, comme s’ils mangeaient leur propre chair \q et s’enivraient de leur propre sang comme de vin. \q Alors tout le monde sur la terre saura que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je suis celui qui te sauve. \q Je suis celui qui te délivre, le Dieu puissant de Jacob.

sw.L: Nami nitawalisha wale wanaokuonea nyama yao wenyewe, \q na kama kwa divai mpya watalewa kwa damu yao wenyewe; \q na wote wenye mwili watajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mwokozi wako, \q na Mkombozi wako, Mwenye Nguvu wa Yakobo.
sw.B: Wanaokuonea nitawalisha nyama yao wenyewe, \q nao watalewa kwa damu yao wenyewe kana kwamba ni divai mpya. \q Ndipo wanadamu wote watajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ndiye ninayekuokoa, \q Mkombozi wako, Mwenye Nguvu wa Yakobo.
sw.R: Nitawafanya watu wanaokuumiza wajiangamize wenyewe, kana kwamba wanakula nyama yao wenyewe \q na kulewa kwa damu yao wenyewe kama divai. \q Ndipo kila mtu duniani atajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ndiye ninayekuokoa. \q Mimi ni Mkombozi wako, Mungu Mwenye Nguvu wa Yakobo.

decisions.choice: eat their own flesh, drunk on their own blood: the oppressors destroy themselves
decisions.reason: The same picture describes a people tearing itself apart in 9:19-20 and Zechariah 11:9. Those who devoured Zion (verse 19) will devour themselves.

decisions.choice: the Mighty One of Jacob: an ancient title of God
decisions.reason: The title comes from Jacob's blessing of Joseph (Genesis 49:24) and is used in Psalm 132:2, 5. Isaiah 1:24 has "the Mighty One of Israel", and 60:16 repeats this whole line.

decisions.choice: all flesh: all humankind
decisions.reason: "Flesh" means every human being, as in 40:5, where all flesh sees the LORD's glory.

decisions.choice: destroy themselves, as if
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means and marks it as a picture.

decisions.choice: el Poderoso de Jacob
decisions.reason: The ancient title of Genesis 49:24 and Psalm 132:2, 5, in its published Spanish form, at every level.

decisions.choice: Mwenye Nguvu wa Yakobo (Literal, Balanced); Mungu Mwenye Nguvu wa Yakobo (Readable)
decisions.reason: The ancient title in its published form (Genesis 49:24; Psalm 132:2); Readable adds "Mungu" so that the title is plainly God's.

decisions.choice: "le Puissant de Jacob" (L, B), "le Dieu puissant de Jacob" (R)
decisions.reason: As Psalm 132:2; Readable names him as God. Settled for chapters 41-66.
